q: How many FTE does each point of virtual-agent containment free up?

r.response:
On the 2,000-FTE, 29-contract contact-centre estate, each point of virtual-agent containment frees about 18 FTE — about 90 FTE for every 5 points.

• Containment is 18% in month 3 of the 5-month adoption plan, across about 1,200 customer intents
• The saving is net of fall-back demand: contacts the virtual agent starts but cannot finish come back to an advisor with about 35% longer handle time
• A contained session costs about £0.38 against £4.10 for an advisor-handled call

Across the group's wider contact-handling workforce, one point is worth about £2.4M a year. Released FTE are best redeployed to casework backlogs before any exit decisions.

q: What does 40% virtual-agent containment do to operating margin?

r.response:
At 40% virtual-agent containment — up from 18% in the budget — FY2026 adjusted operating profit rises from £119.7M to about £171M, and the margin from 6.5% to 9.3%.

• Each point of containment saves about £2.4M of advisor cost, net of fall-back demand and virtual-agent session cost
• 22 points release roughly 1,900 FTE-equivalent across the group's contact-handling workforce — capacity for casework backlogs, new contracts or natural attrition
• Revenue is unchanged in this lever: fixed-price and per-transaction contracts keep the saving unless gainshare clauses apply

Combined with +8% volume and 94% KPI attainment, the AI-Led Delivery scenario reaches about £205M (10.5%).
